html:
The Orange Free State was an independent Boer republic between the Orange and Vaal rivers in southern Africa, from 1854 to 1902. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Its people were mostly Voortrekkers of the Great Trek and their families, Dutch-speaking farmers who had left the British Cape Colony. Britain ruled the area briefly as the Orange River Sovereignty from 1848, then gave it up in 1854.

The republic fought the Basotho of Moshoeshoe in the 1850s and 1860s and took much of their farmland, until Britain made Basutoland a protectorate. It claimed the diamond fields found in 1871, but Britain annexed them as Griqualand West.

The Free State was a quiet, well-run farming republic, but it stood by its ally the Transvaal in the Second Boer War. British troops took Bloemfontein in 1900, and the republic became the Orange River Colony. In 1910 it joined the Union of South Africa.
